communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: DRMM monitoring (updated)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All completed programmatic monitoring reports, completed monitoring checklists or tools, corrective action plans, provider responses to corrective actions, and follow-up or verification reports prepared or maintained by the City of Detroit Human, Homeless, and Family Services Department concerning Detroit Rescue Mission Ministries from January 1, 2026 through the date of this request.

This request is a resubmission of FOIA request 2603656 (attached). In the City’s August 7, 2026 response, the City stated that the requested reports were “still in the process of being completed” and asked that the request be resubmitted at a later date.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Aaron Mondry

title: Federal Enclave Status of Arlington National Cemetery.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I work as a research analyst for the Laborers International Union of North America.  I have a question regarding the federal enclave status of Arlington National Cemetery.   I have been researching online whether Arlington National Cemetery has been formally designated as a federal enclave.  I came across a report that the General Services Administration conducted in 1962 titled "Inventory Report on Jurisdictional Status of Federal Areas within States" [see attached PDF file, Appendix A].  It contains an inventory report on the jurisdictional status of federal areas within states.  It ranks the jurisdictional status of each federal area on a scale of "1" (the strongest status, meaning exclusive legislative jurisdiction for the federal government) to a "5" (the weakest status for the feds).

This inventory ranks Arlington National Cemetery's jurisdictional status as a "1".  The definition of a jurisdictional status of  a "1" is as follows:

“Exclusive Legislative Jurisdiction. This term is applied when the federal government possesses, by whichever method acquired, all the authority of the State, and in which the State concerned has not reserved to itself the right to exercise any of the authority concurrently with the United States except the right to serve civil or criminal process in the area for activities which occurred outside the area.”



Does the GSA inventory listing Arlington National Cemetery's federal jurisdictional status as a "1" constitute clear proof that Arlington National Cemetery is a designated federal enclave?



You can reach me at the listed email address. Thanks for your attention to this matter.



Sincerely,





Glenn Daigon

Research Analyst

Laborers International Union

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Glenn Daigon
